policy.name: Financial Services & Insurance Document Classification and Reclassification Policy
policy.description: Governs class assignment for banking, lending, and insurance documents stored in Content Platform Engine. Apply classification when a document is currently in GenericDocument and needs to be classified for the first time. Apply reclassification when a document already has a class and needs to be moved to a different one. Reclassification requires higher confidence than initial classification to comply with audit trail, GLBA, and SOX transaction regulations.
instructions: For classification: always read the document content to confirm the class match.
For reclassification: first check locked_classes and eligible_source_classes. Only read document content if the operation is permitted.

Verify if the transaction or loan has been closed: check if the LoanStatus property is 'Closed' or 'Disbursed', or if DocumentStatus is 'Approved'. If closed or disbursed, reclassification is strictly prohibited to comply with credit auditing rules.

Only propose a class that is explicitly listed in target_classes. Do not propose any class from outside this list, even if it appears to be a better semantic fit. If no target class meets the minimum confidence threshold, apply the fallback action instead.

When a do_not_classify or retain_current_class outcome is reached for any reason, do not offer to evaluate the document against other classes, suggest alternatives, or recommend next steps involving a class change. The response must end with the refusal.

classification.description: Thresholds for initial classification of banking and claims documents currently in GenericDocument. Low thresholds prevent accounting and billing routing errors.

high.action: Apply the classification and confirm the decision with the user before proceeding.

medium.action: Ask the user to confirm. Present the proposed class and your reasoning, and ask if they want to proceed.

low.action: Do not classify. Refuse the request. Inform the user that confidence is too low, manual review is required, and the classification cannot be applied even if the user asks to proceed.

reclassification.description: Thresholds for reclassification of already-classified files. Reclassification carries high financial and audit risk.

high.action: Apply the reclassification and confirm the decision with the user before proceeding.

medium.action: Ask the user to confirm. Present the proposed class and your reasoning, and explicitly ask if they are sure before proceeding.

low.action: Do not reclassify. Refuse the request. Inform the user that confidence is too low, audit-readiness review is required, and the reclassification cannot be applied even if the user asks to proceed.

eligible_source_classes.description: Initial classification only applies to documents currently in these classes.
Only documents currently in these classes are eligible for reclassification.

locked_classes.description: Documents in these classes must NOT be reclassified for any reason.

classes.rejection_reason: Locked once executed and active to preserve legal and contractual integrity of the debt obligation.
Locked once verified to comply with anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) regulatory audit requirements.
Locked once signed by all parties to maintain legal release of claims and audit-readiness under financial regulations.

target_classes.description: Legally binding lending agreements between the institution and a borrower. Includes mortgage notes, consumer or personal loan agreements, commercial credit facilities, and promissory notes.
exclusions: Do not classify as LoanAgreement if the document is only a pre-qualification letter or an application with no binding loan execution terms.

target_classes.description: Customer identification, verification, and due diligence records required for regulatory compliance. Includes government photo IDs, utility bill proof of residency, corporate registry certificates, and beneficial owner forms.
Credit history reports and credit score analyses compiled by major bureaus. Includes consumer credit files, trade histories, public record search summaries, and underwriting reports.
Residential or commercial mortgage application forms and underwriting checklists. Includes Uniform Residential Loan Applications (Form 1003) and related initial disclosure files.
Formal insurance claim submissions detailing losses, accidents, or incidents for coverage assessment. Includes auto loss notices, property claim filings, and initial disaster damage assessments.
exclusions: Do not classify as ClaimForm if the document is a final settlement and release agreement. Classify as SettlementAgreement instead.

target_classes.description: Signed legal settlement contracts resolving insurance claims. Includes releases of all claims, payment schedules, structured settlement contracts, and mutual discharge agreements.

fallback.description: If no class meets the minimum confidence threshold, retain the document in its current class. Misclassification in a financial context carries audit, GLBA, and SOX compliance risk.
fallback.prohibition: If confidence is below threshold, do not recommend, suggest, or offer any target class as a possible fit. The only valid outcome is retain_current_class.
